newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-BOWLERS GIVE EARLY EDGE TO SRI LANKA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BOWLERS GIVE EARLY EDGE TO SRI LANKA.

text.p: Paceman Chaminda Vaas claimed two quick wickets just before lunch to seize the initiative for Sri Lanka after the hosts were all out for 331 in their first innings on the second day of the second test against Pakistan on Sunday.
Vaas bowled a tight length and had both Salim Elahi and Ijaz Ahmed, who scored a century for Pakistan in the first test, caught at slips, shattering the visitors' hopes of making a strong start.
Elahi, who was out first ball to Vaas in the first test match, could do no better this time and played only four balls before being caught at slip by Hashan Tillekeratne for nought.
Izaj became Vaas's second victim when he edged the ball to Arnold Russell at third slip for a low catch. He made four runs.
Skipper Ramiz Raja (16) and Salim Malik (9) then took Pakistan to lunch without further loss.
Earlier Sri Lanka, resuming at 281 for 7, added 50 runs to their overnight total before being dismissed 35 minutes before lunch for 331.

Vice-captain Aravinda de Silva, who saved Sri Lanka from total collapse on Saturday by hitting a stylish century, remained unbeaten on 138. His chanceless innings was crafted in 273 minutes off 208 balls and included 15 hits to the boundary.

Vaas, who made 17, helped De Silva to add 76 runs for the eighth wicket -- a record for Sri Lanka. The previous best eighth wicket partnership of 73 was between Vaas and Kumara Dharmasena against Zimbabwe in the 1996-97 home series.
After Vaas left, caught by Elahi off Saqlain's bowling, Aravinda De Silva was left standing alone as the last two batsmen fell without scoring.
Saqlain Mushtaq, who took nine wickets in the first test, was again the star for Pakistan, claiming four wickets for 115 runs in 45 overs.
Scores: Sri Lanka 331, Pakistan 30 for 2 at lunch.
